info_invalid_json.title: Stored mapping is not a valid JSON array
info_invalid_json.text: The table stays empty as long as the stored value cannot be parsed. Repair it via the command line. Caution: entering a row in the table replaces the stored value and discards the unparsable content.
info_invalid_json.hidden: try { return Array.isArray(JSON.parse(data.mappingsRaw || '[]')); } catch (e) { return false; }

mappingsTable.label: Couplings
mappingsTable.defaultFunc: try { const v = JSON.parse(data.mappingsRaw || '[]'); return Array.isArray(v) ? v : undefined; } catch (e) { return undefined; }

items.title: ID
items.tooltip: Handle of this coupling. It names the channels.<id> datapoints (enabled, lastValue). Generated when the row is created; editable, but it must stay unique and may contain only letters, digits, _ and - (no dots).
items.validatorErrorText: Required: letters, digits, _ or - (max 32, no dots)

items.title: Source
items.validatorErrorText: Required: a state ID without blanks, without a leading/trailing dot and without '..'

items.title: Target
items.validatorErrorText: Required: a state ID without blanks, without a leading/trailing dot and without '..'

items.title: Enabled
items.tooltip: Startup strategy for this coupling's enabled datapoint, applied at every adapter start. yes/no force it (a runtime change then lasts until the next start), (def) forces the adapter default from the Adapter-Settings tab, (keep) leaves an existing datapoint alone — use (keep) if you want to switch this coupling at runtime. A missing datapoint is always created from the adapter default.

items.title: on ACK
items.tooltip: Forward on ACK: relay when the source carries ack=true (device confirmations), not only commands. (def) = adapter default.

items.title: on change
items.tooltip: Forward value changes only: skip re-writes of an unchanged value (e.g. polling refreshes). (def) = adapter default.

items.title: pass ACK
items.tooltip: Propagate the ACK flag: write the target with the source's ack instead of ack=false (command semantics). (def) = adapter default.

legend_columns.text: ID names this coupling's datapoints under channels.<id> — generated automatically, editable, must stay unique · One source may feed several targets (fan-out); bidirectional branches are allowed, but a value written back by one branch reaches the others only through the periodic sync — the log says so at every start · Enabled = startup strategy for this coupling's switch: yes/no force it at every start, (def) forces the adapter default, (keep) leaves the runtime datapoint alone · Per-entry filters: (def) = use the adapter default from the Adapter-Settings tab · on ACK = relay also when the source carries ack=true · on change = skip re-writes of an unchanged value · pass ACK = write the target with the source's ack flag instead of ack=false

mappingsRaw.label: Mappings (JSON view, read-only)
mappingsRaw.help: Canonical storage form, read-only — the table above is the editor and its changes are written back here. Use the copy button to export the JSON.

onChange.calculateFunc: return data.mappingsTable === undefined ? data.mappingsRaw : JSON.stringify(data.mappingsTable, null, 2);

syncIntervalValue.label: Interval
syncIntervalValue.help: 0 = disabled. When set, all target datapoints are re-written at this interval with the last known source value (heartbeat/refresh). Only the forward direction (source → target) is synced; the reverse direction of bidirectional entries is not included in periodic updates.

relayOnChange.label: Also relay on change (in addition to periodic sync)
relayOnChange.help: When periodic sync is active (interval > 0), also relay immediately on source value change. Has no effect when interval is 0 — event-driven relay is always active then.

hdr_defaults.text: Relay defaults are applied to all mapping entries unless overridden per entry.

enabledDefault.label: Enable flag default
enabledDefault.help: Initial state of the per-channel enabled datapoint. Can be overridden per entry via the 'enabled' field of the mapping entry and toggled at runtime via the channels.<id>.enabled datapoints.

hdr_coerce.text: Type coercion casts the source value to the target datapoint's type before writing. Only acts on type mismatch; matching types are passed through unchanged.

coerceTypesDefault.label: Coerce types (bool ↔ number, C convention)
coerceTypesDefault.help: Cast between boolean and number following C conventions: number 0 → false / non-0 → true, false → 0 / true → 1. Applied on both event relay and periodic sync.

coerceStringsDefault.label: Also interpret strings
coerceStringsDefault.help: Additionally interpret strings when coercing: ""/"0"/"false" → false, else → true; numeric strings → number. Unrecognized strings are passed through unchanged. Off by default (extra effort, opt-in).
